scenes.narration: Pablo Escobar's hippos are still alive, and Colombia has approved killing some of them. In 1981, he imported four of them for his private zoo.
scenes.main_point: Open on the man, then the animals.
scenes.visual_objective: Show Pablo Escobar's own police photograph before explaining the story.
scenes.animation: headline slides in; photograph never moves; evidence lines arrive in turn

scenes.narration: His estate lay between Medellín and Bogotá.
scenes.visual_objective: Place Hacienda Nápoles between Medellín and Bogotá on a drawn map of Colombia.
scenes.animation: country tints, route and pins draw on, labels slide in

scenes.narration: After he died in 1993, they escaped and spread. By 2007 there were sixteen, by 2014 about forty, and now around two hundred.
scenes.visual_objective: Show a real hippo at Hacienda Nápoles and the counts as they grew.
scenes.animation: photograph holds still; accent circle draws on; count lines arrive in turn

scenes.narration: In April 2026, Colombia approved killing more than eighty of them. An Indian billionaire offered to take them to India instead.
scenes.visual_objective: State the cull number large, then the date, the ministry and the offer from India.
scenes.animation: number slides in; evidence lines arrive in turn

scenes.narration: Most conservationists call them invasive, but some ecologists say they should stay. So who decides what happens to Escobar's hippos?
scenes.visual_objective: Return to the estate and set the two views side by side, labelled as the article gives them.
